articles.title: AI 数据中心挤占成熟制程产能，汽车芯片供应链面临瓶颈
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，据路透社报道，安世半导体临时首席执行官斯特凡 · 蒂尔格（Stefan Tilger）周二在慕尼黑举行的 Electronica 电子展上接受采访时表示，随着供应商将制造产能转向快速增长的 AI 数据中心市场，减少对汽车和工业设备所用成熟制程芯片的投入，安世半导体目前的订单已经“完全超额”。蒂尔格表示，部分竞争对手已经将产能从安世半导体供应的通用型半导体产品转移出去，导致汽车供应链的部分环节出现瓶颈。他在采访中说：“目前，汽车行业正受到相当严重的冲击。”IT之家注意到，意法半导体（STMicroelectronics）首席执行官让-马克 · 谢里（Jean-Marc Chery）周一也发出警告称，晶圆代工厂和芯片封装企业正越来越多地将资源从汽车和工业应用产品转向其他领域。谢里在展会开幕前举行的首席执行官圆桌会议上表示：“我们看到了许多供应瓶颈。”这些表态进一步表明，AI 投资热潮正在给半导体供应链的其他领域带来压力。随着制造商优先生产与数据中心和人工智能相关、利润率更高的产品，传统芯片的供应也受到影响。谢里表示，一些过去服务于广泛客户群体的晶圆代工厂、芯片组装和封装企业，正在逐渐退出主流技术领域。蒂尔格指出，AI 数据中心和机器人领域的需求正在大量消耗制造产能，而用于二极管、晶体管及其他基础元器件的成熟技术，多年来一直缺乏足够投资。安世半导体主要生产大批量、低成本的半导体产品，客户集中在汽车和工业设备领域。与意法半导体等大型竞争对手不同，安世半导体的产品线相对狭窄，主要专注于成熟制程元器件。谢里则表示，意法半导体拥有自己的制造体系，因此在一定程度上能够抵御供应限制带来的冲击。他说：“通过资本支出和自身制造能力，我们能够掌握一部分未来的主动权。”

articles.title: 24Gb GDDR7 价格过高，传 16GB 版本 GeForce RTX 5080 显卡回归市场
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，渠道消息平台 博板堂 版主 高手一号 昨日爆料称，NVIDIA（英伟达）已向 AIC 合作伙伴通知放弃 2027 年 1 月上市 GeForce RTX 5080 24GB 显卡，这一型号暂无明确的上市排期。消息人士宣称，此番搁置的本质原因还是单颗粒 24Gb (3GB) 的 GDDR7 显存价格仍处于高位，导致整卡成本结构难以满足商业化的需求。随着 24GB 版本的延后乃至取消，16GB 版本的 GeForce RTX 5080 也会再次启用，满足市场对同等级产品的需求。

articles.title: 东安动力：预计全年增程器销量占比超 30%，产能可满足车厂需求
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，据《证券时报》，东安动力在 2026 年第三季度业绩说明会上披露，公司作为国内最早实现增程器商业化的企业，持续深耕增程新能源市场。东安动力披露，伴随客户项目的陆续批产上市，增程器销量占比不断提高，全年销量占比预计超过 30%；产品主要配套企业包括小米汽车、小鹏汽车、岚图汽车、江淮汽车等车企，现在产能可以满足车厂需求。IT之家从东安动力公布的财报获悉，2026 年前三季度，东安动力实现营业收入 36.54 亿元，同比下降 2.98%；毛利润 1.41 亿元，同比增长 26.43%；毛利率 3.87%，同比提高 0.90 个百分点。同期归母净亏损 8388.19 万元；扣非归母净亏损 1.21 亿元。集团前三季度营业亏损 7492.49 万元。第三季度单季营业收入 11.72 亿元，同比下降 8.97%；归母净亏损 7494.72 万元，扣非归母净亏损 9232.62 万元。公司指出，产品结构变化及产品降价导致当季毛利率下降，对盈利形成压力。

articles.title: 京东物流首次开通西藏班列，4000 米高原快递坐火车出藏最快“次日达”
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，京东今日宣布，近日，京东物流拉萨 — 西宁铁路班列正式开通。这一班列沿着青藏铁路，经停那曲、安多、雁石坪、沱沱河、不冻泉等地，单程 20.5 小时，主要承运西藏特产和消费品。这是京东物流首次在西藏开通铁路班列，开通后，快递进出西藏时效较此前平均提前 2 天，出藏最快可“次日达”。IT之家获悉，在开通西藏铁路班列之外，京东物流还同步推出“空转陆”服务，西藏至成都段空运，成都至下一目的地陆运。相比全程空运服务，价格降低超五成，低至 9 元 / Kg；相比全程陆运服务，时效大幅提升，最快次日达。据介绍，拉萨智能仓配备了 100 余台自研的“地狼”搬运机器人，拣选效率较人工提升近 3 倍。今年开仓的林芝前置智能仓，可支持主城区实现“211 限时达”，松茸、林芝苹果、藏天麻等农特产品可就近备货、直发全国。目前，京东物流常态化运行的铁路运输线路已超 700 条。今年下半年以来，陆续开通了京津冀至粤港澳大湾区“京东号”电商集装箱班列、长三角至京津冀电商多式联运快速班列。

articles.title: 我国加快推进“人工智能+自然资源”深度融合，计划 2030 年集成打造智能化国土空间治理基础平台
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，自然资源部、国家发展改革委近日发布关于“人工智能 + 自然资源”的实施意见，加快推动人工智能在自然资源领域规模化、产业化创新应用，服务国土空间规划“一张图”智能化升级。其中，意见明确分阶段发展目标：到 2028 年，实现人工智能在自然资源领域的示范应用，建成时空地理信息、国土空间规划与治理、海洋、地质矿产、林业草原等重点方向的高质量数据集、大模型和智能体，“一张图”智能化水平全面提升，形成可复制、可推广的典型应用场景，助推自然资源新质生产力发展。到 2030 年，人工智能深度融入自然资源管理全链条，集成打造智能化国土空间治理基础平台，关键核心技术与智能装备实现安全可控，自然资源数智化治理水平总体达到国际领先，人工智能成为引领生态文明建设与高质量发展的重要引擎。IT之家注意到，意见提出统筹布局五个人工智能中试平台，覆盖时空地理信息、国土空间规划与治理、海洋、地质矿产、林草方向，打造集算力供给、模型训练、算法迭代、场景验证和生态构建于一体的共性服务体系。意见同步还推出八大示范场景，涵盖“天空地海网”一体化监测、智慧国土空间规划、自然资源资产管理、自然资源灾害治理等。

articles.title: 佳能发布 KrF 半导体光刻机 FPA-6400ES6a，宣称实现高生产率和业界高水平套刻精度
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，11 月 10 日，佳能在日本东京宣布，将于 2026 年 12 月上旬发售面向存储和逻辑芯片的 KrF（IT之家注：氟化氪）扫描式半导体光刻机“FPA-6400ES6a”。▲ KrF 扫描式半导体光刻机“FPA-6400ES6a”官方表示，通过新开发的超高加速度载台缩短驱动时间，这款 KrF 扫描式半导体光刻机新产品具备每小时 400 片晶圆的高产能；同时新开发了即使在高速驱动时也能进行稳定高精度位置控制的震动抑制技术，以及降低设备内气流不均匀、使激光光路温度均一化的空调控制技术，从而实现业界高水平的 4.0nm 套刻精度。此外，在佳能独有的图像对准系统中，新增了可选配的新光源“Hi-ALS（High Alignment Light Source）”。由于可根据材料和工艺任意选择合适的对准测量波长，因此能在各种半导体制造工艺中实现高精度对准，提高工艺稳定性。同时，设备可在曝光前测量各种工艺中产生的晶圆翘曲量，并通过调整载台上的吸气流量，提高对大翘曲晶圆的吸附能力，从而改善曝光时的翘曲。由此，可对应的翘曲量扩大到 700μm，强化了对三维器件的堆叠及晶圆键合工艺中产生的晶圆翘曲的应对能力。▲ 晶圆翘曲改善的示意图（改善前与改善后）据介绍，佳能半导体光刻机“FPA-6400ES6a”搭载新开发的电力控制技术，可将在载台减速时产生的再生电力储存在电容器中，并在加速时加以再利用。通过控制来自电源和电容器的电力供给，在确保超高加速度载台所需高响应性的同时，有效利用再生能源。该设备还配备了新开发的支持超高加速度载台的高效率电源，通过提升电源效率降低电力损耗，并简化冷却机构。通过这些技术，降低了每片晶圆曝光所需的耗电量，同时兼顾了环境保护。

articles.title: 林肯中国总裁贾鸣镝：全新车型飞行家 EX8 将于明年上半年上市
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，据“新车情报局”，在今天（11 日）的林肯汽车沟通会上，林肯中国总裁贾鸣镝披露了林肯全新车型的更多消息：新车命名为林肯飞行家 EX8，定位林肯全球首款豪华智擎超混车型。他透露，新车造型设计和体量感“更像领航员”，但由于尺寸更接近飞行家，所以选择沿用了飞行家的名字。值得一提的是，这也是林肯首次选用中国的命名提案。至于“EX8”三个字母，则是用来体现车型的市场定位。E 代表新能源、X 代表 SUV 的多功能性、8 代表 8 系大五座。产品规划方面，新车将会在 2026 广州车展亮相，明年上半年上市。就在本月早些时候，工信部发布第 413 批《道路机动车辆生产企业及产品公告》新产品公示，长安福特汽车有限公司的林肯飞行家 AVIATOR EX8 完成申报。IT之家从申报信息获悉，此次申报的车型长宽高分别为 5055/1995/1790 或 1800mm，轴距 3010mm，定位中大型豪华 SUV。轮胎规格提供 255/50R21 与 255/45R22 两种选择，额定载客人数为 5 人。动力方面，新车搭载由重庆长安汽车股份有限公司生产的型号为 JL469ZQ1 的 1.5T 发动机，排量 1497ml，额定功率 110kW，发动机最大净功率为 105kW。车辆支持纯电动模式行驶，最高车速可达 205km/h。储能装置采用磷酸铁锂蓄电池，电池单体及总成均由时代长安动力电池有限公司提供。两款车型的整备质量分别为 2580kg 与 2480kg，总质量对应为 2980kg 与 2870kg。

articles.title: 芬兰批准特斯拉辅助驾驶系统 TAD 上路使用，成为第 11 个放行的欧洲国家
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，据路透社报道，芬兰交通与通信局（Traficom）当地时间周三表示，特斯拉辅助驾驶系统 Tesla Assisted Driving（TAD）已获准在芬兰道路上使用。至此，芬兰成为继拉脱维亚之后第 11 个批准该系统的欧洲国家。该机构在声明中称，这意味着特斯拉可以立即开始向芬兰用户提供这套系统，符合条件的车辆也可以在芬兰道路上启用该功能。今年 6 月，芬兰曾表示，可能在欧盟层面作出统一决定之前，率先批准特斯拉这套系统。目前，欧盟范围内的相关审批仍在等待结果。IT之家注意到，今年 4 月，荷兰成为欧洲首个临时批准该系统的国家。这项审批被视为推动该技术未来在欧盟范围内推广的第一步，但欧盟范围内的统一推广仍需获得成员国特定多数支持。此后，爱沙尼亚、克罗地亚和比利时等国也陆续允许这项技术在当地投入使用。该系统能够在驾驶员监督下控制车辆转向，不过部分监管机构仍对其安全性和使用条件持谨慎态度。Traficom 表示：“该机构认可了荷兰主管部门授予的临时整车型式批准，因此特斯拉辅助驾驶系统可以作为驾驶辅助系统在芬兰使用。”这套系统最初以 FSD（Supervised）为名，11 月 3 日，荷兰车辆管理局（RDW）批准了特斯拉对系统的部分调整，包括将名称改为 Tesla Assisted Driving，并将允许的速度偏移幅度从此前最高 50% 限制为 10%，每次启动车辆时默认恢复为 0%。RDW 明确表示，更名不会改变系统性质，驾驶员仍然承担驾驶责任。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，海关统计数据显示，今年前 10 个月，经港珠澳大桥珠海公路口岸通过海关跨境电商管理平台出口达 1120 亿元，同比增长 33.1%，已超 2025 年全年。目前，经港珠澳大桥珠海公路口岸出口的包裹日均超 300 万个，覆盖全球 200 多个国家和地区。据IT之家此前报道，今年 6 月，港珠澳大桥香港口岸推出 2 条“无感 e-道”。通关人员完成登记后，系统将通过容貌识别与人工智能影像分析技术核验身份，全程无需驻足，仅约 5 秒即可完成出境手续，较传统“e-道”提速约 2 秒。此外，截至今年 5 月 25 日上午 11 时 50 分，经港珠澳大桥珠海公路口岸出入境港澳单牌车总量正式突破 1000 万辆次。

articles.title: 红果短剧上线 AI 剧虚拟形象确权功能
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，红果短剧创作者中心 11 月 9 日发布《AI 剧虚拟形象创编与确权能力上线公告》。公告指出，在 AI 剧虚拟形象创作中，形象可能来源于真人授权、上游 IP 授权或原创创作，涉及肖像、美术设计等多类权益。为帮助各位创作者前置上传权属材料，避免后续发布作品受到影响，平台现提供“虚拟形象创编与确权”能力支持。公告内容提到，如版权人已取得真人授权或上游 IP 授权，或已具备著作权登记证书等权属材料，可在平台提报对应虚拟形象及相关材料申请确权。平台将对提交信息进行审核，审核通过后会形成确权记录，供后续内容使用与风险处置环节参考。公告特别说明，确权记录用于辅助权属信息留存，不代表对内容或权益风险的绝对兜底；内容上线及分发仍需符合平台规则及相关法律法规要求。今年 10 月，红果短剧官方发布关于持续加强低质和同质化内容治理的公告，为维护健康、多元、可持续的创作环境，平台将进一步加大对低质和同质化内容的治理力度，重点治理过度情绪渲染和对微短剧剧情结构、核心设定、关键桥段、人物关系及视听表达要素的同质化使用问题。主要包括以下三种场景：一、刻意渲染矛盾为片面追逐流量，刻意渲染矛盾，放大家庭、邻里、职场等场景中的冲突分歧，剧情推进缺少合理铺垫和人物塑造，机械堆叠反转、争吵等刺激性桥段，缺少正向叙事价值。二、剧情内容同质化剧集核心设定、人物关系、关键桥段及剧情推进手法高度相似，仅靠局部细节替换制造差异；或套用固定模板，跨剧集、跨账号批量“换皮”的内容。三、人物素材同质化在人物形象层面，批量套用同一人脸模型、五官模板，导致不同作品、不同角色在脸型、五官、妆造及整体辨识度上高度相似，出现“多人同脸”“跨剧撞脸”等问题。

articles.title: OpenAI 宣布 12 月 11 日停用 ChatGPT 旧版语音模式，全面转向 GPT-Live
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，早在 2024 年，OpenAI 就推出了 Advanced Voice Mode（高级语音模式），让用户能够与 ChatGPT 进行更加自然的语音交流。最初的 Standard Voice Mode（标准语音模式）需要分别通过语音转文字、语言模型和文字转语音等模型完成交互，而 Advanced Voice Mode 可以直接处理和生成音频，因此响应速度更快，对话也更加自然。不过，无论是标准语音模式还是高级语音模式，都采用轮流对话机制，即模型必须等用户说完之后才能作出回应。今年 7 月，OpenAI 推出了新一代语音模型 GPT-Live，采用全双工架构，允许 ChatGPT 在倾听用户说话的同时进行语音回复，从而实现更加自然、流畅的交流。此外，GPT-Live 还能够处理复杂问题，并在不中断当前语音对话的情况下，将相关任务交由 OpenAI 旗下的前沿文本模型完成。OpenAI 表示，自今年 7 月 GPT-Live 发布以来，ChatGPT 的语音功能使用量已接近翻倍。目前，通过语音与 ChatGPT 互动的用户中，大多数已经转向使用 GPT-Live。基于这一变化，OpenAI 今天宣布，将于 2026 年 12 月 11 日正式停用 ChatGPT 中的 Advanced Voice Mode 和 Standard Voice Mode，逐步淘汰这两种旧版语音体验，未来将把开发资源集中在 GPT-Live 上。具体调整时间安排如下：2026 年 11 月 10 日：OpenAI 开始向用户发送旧版语音模式即将停用的通知。即日起至 12 月 11 日：用户仍然可以继续使用 Advanced Voice Mode 和 Standard Voice Mode。2026 年 12 月 11 日：两种旧版语音模式将从 ChatGPT 的“设置-语音”选项中移除。此前选择使用这两种模式的用户将自动切换至 GPT-Live。历史对话方面：此前的语音对话记录仍会保留在 ChatGPT 历史记录中，用户可以继续通过文字或 GPT-Live 接续这些对话。不过，此次调整也存在一些例外。由于 GPT-Live 目前尚不支持实时视频和屏幕共享功能，ChatGPT 的这两项功能仍将继续使用 Advanced Voice Mode。此外，用户与自定义 GPT 进行语音对话时，也会继续使用 Advanced Voice Mode，直至 12 月 11 日。IT之家注意到，OpenAI 淘汰旧版语音模式的决定并未得到所有用户的认可。在 X 平台和 Reddit 社区中，不少 ChatGPT 用户表达了不满。部分用户认为，Standard Voice Mode 能够提供更加详细的回答，而且与文字对话之间的上下文衔接也更好。相比之下，GPT-Live 经常打断用户说话、丢失对话上下文，或者给出不够实用的回答。一些付费订阅用户甚至表示，如果 OpenAI 坚持执行这一决定，他们将考虑取消订阅。OpenAI 承认，部分用户可能更喜欢 Advanced Voice Mode 或 Standard Voice Mode 的回答风格。公司表示，正在吸收旧版模型的经验，进一步改善 GPT-Live 的回答深度、对话连贯性和个性化表现。接下来值得关注的是，面对用户的强烈反对，OpenAI 是否会重新考虑这项决定。此前，OpenAI 曾因用户反对而决定暂缓停用 GPT-4o。当时公司也面临类似的舆论压力，最终推迟了原定的退役计划。

articles.title: 阿维塔 1300 台「战损车基地」曝光，副总裁雍军曾透露价值约 6 个亿
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，阿维塔科技官方今日曝光了其 1300 台「战损车基地」，阿维塔科技副总裁雍军此前在直播中透露，该基地价值约 6 个亿。阿维塔官方还宣布，将在 11 月 12 日在现场进行直播，介绍战损车基地的情况。雍军昨日发文表示，汽车研发没有捷径，研发测试的钱一分都不能省。阿维塔坚决不造速成车，车一旦速成，一个家庭没了的可能性就会增大。参考IT之家此前报道，工业和信息化部等四部门 10 月 10 日公开发布关于进一步加强汽车产品创新设计和研发测试验证有关管理工作的通知（征求意见稿）。此次出台的文件重点面向三个方向：一是研发测试验证，明确测试周期和里程的硬性要求。新申报产品必须完成综合可靠性与耐久性、结构可靠性、软件功能可靠性等测试。其中，环境适应性验证周期不少于 1 年，须包含“两冬一夏”试验；可靠性验证试验里程不低于 3 万公里。二是创新设计准入，划出红线清单。禁止配备全隐藏式车门把手；不得采用折叠屏、柔性屏；行车过程中不得使用“零重力”座椅、旋转座椅或座椅放倒成床等功能；应急逃生、应急制动等涉及安全的操纵件必须保留实体操纵件和醒目标识。三是准入管理，明确执行时间和处置措施。自 2027 年 1 月 1 日起，未按要求进行测试验证、验证不充分或提供虚假材料的产品不予公告；已取得公告的产品须在 2027 年 7 月 1 日前补报相关材料，逾期且存在安全隐患的，停止生产并实施召回。

articles.title: Allianz CIO Says Markets Are Underestimating Inflation Surge
articles.content: Allianz Chief Investment Officer and Chief Economist Ludovic Subran says, "The second inflation shock is not sized properly, not only by markets, but by policymakers." He speaks on Bloomberg Television after US short-term bond yields surged by the most in 19 months on a faster-than-expected rise in consumer prices and warnings by Federal Reserve officials that interest rates may need to be hiked more aggressively. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: B 社：未来一段时间内不会有《上古卷轴 6：哨兵》的新消息
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，贝塞斯达（Bethesda）近日在 Reddit 论坛表示，他们不会在 11 月 11 日发布任何重大公告，并且未来一段时间内也不会有《上古卷轴 6：哨兵》游戏的新消息。据IT之家了解，近期曾有部分海外博主声称，他们从 B 社内部人士打探到消息，说《上古卷轴 5：天际》发售 15 年（本作于 2011 年 11 月 11 日发售）之际会有重大情报出现。同时，B 社于 11 月 3 日发布的工作室成立 40 周年纪念视频中暗示，《上古卷轴 6：哨兵》的剧情可能发生在锤落省。除此之外，相关内容并没有透露《上古卷轴 6》新消息。此外，彭博社记者杰森 · 施赖尔近日曾表示，《上古卷轴 6：哨兵》不会在最近两年正式亮相，他认为本作 2029 年发售是比较现实的。

articles.title: 玛莎拉蒂将在迪拜打造品牌住宅岛：配游艇接驳、海上餐厅，首批住宅 2030 年交付
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，玛莎拉蒂这次把三叉戟标志从汽车引擎盖搬到了住宅大门上。当地时间 2026 年 11 月 9 日，意大利豪华汽车制造商玛莎拉蒂与迪拜房地产开发商 Samana Collecta 联合宣布，将在迪拜海岸附近的“世界群岛”项目中打造一座品牌住宅岛，命名为“玛莎拉蒂岛”（Maserati Island）。这是玛莎拉蒂首次涉足全年居住型房地产项目。根据双方公布的信息，玛莎拉蒂岛计划建设 840 套品牌住宅，首批住宅预计从 2030 年开始交付。整个项目规划了三种住宅类型，包括普通品牌公寓、7 栋水上别墅和 2 栋树屋别墅，所有住宅均冠以玛莎拉蒂品牌名称。双方在联合发布会上表示，首批推出 232 套住宅，户型从单间公寓到四居室不等，每套住宅均配备私人泳池。所有住宅都以无遮挡海景为核心设计理念，通过大面积玻璃窗和开放式户型，将周围的泻湖与海岸景观融入室内空间。室内家具则采用 Giorgetti Maserati Edition 系列产品。这是玛莎拉蒂与意大利家具品牌 Giorgetti 于 2025 年开启的合作项目。阿尔法 · 罗密欧和玛莎拉蒂首席执行官桑托 · 菲奇利（Santo Ficili）表示：“通过玛莎拉蒂岛，我们在 Casa Maserati 开启的品牌发展道路上迈出了重要一步，将我们对意大利奢华生活方式的构想，转化为一种独特的居住体验。”Samana Developers 首席执行官伊姆兰 · 法鲁克（Imran Farooq）则将此次合作称为“一个具有里程碑意义的项目，不仅对 Samana Collecta 如此，对整个迪拜豪华房地产市场也是如此”。玛莎拉蒂首席营销官兼 Bottegafuoriserie 总经理克里斯蒂亚诺 · 菲奥里奥（Cristiano Fiorio）则将这一项目与品牌百年历史联系起来。他表示，随着玛莎拉蒂三叉戟标志迎来诞生 100 周年，玛莎拉蒂岛的推出“标志着品牌历史上的一个重要里程碑”。除了住宅本身，岛上还将配备一系列公共设施，包括中央泻湖、私人海滩、海滩俱乐部、健康与健身设施、水上运动码头，以及一艘停泊在近海的意大利主题水上餐厅。此外，项目还将设置商务办公空间，并提供高速网络连接，方便需要远程办公的住户。岛屿与迪拜大陆之间不会通过桥梁连接。根据中东建筑行业媒体 Construction Business News Middle East 的报道，Samana 计划提供游艇接驳服务，班次间隔为 30 分钟。不过，目前迪拜大陆上的具体登船地点尚未公布。目前，玛莎拉蒂岛住宅的具体售价和销售时间表均未披露。项目预计从 2030 年开始交付，整体开发周期约为 4 年。这一时间安排与迈阿密的布加迪品牌住宅（Bugatti Residences）等豪华汽车品牌房地产项目较为接近。IT之家注意到，近年来玛莎拉蒂正不断将品牌影响力延伸至汽车销售之外，涉足与品牌历史相关的电影制作、酒店服务以及其他生活方式合作项目。此次推出品牌住宅岛，是其拓展品牌商业版图的一次更直接尝试：玛莎拉蒂希望消费者不仅愿意为车头上的三叉戟标志买单，也愿意为家门口的同一个标志支付溢价。

articles.title: 消息称 OpenAI 今年 Q3 营收首次达百亿美元，环比大增近 50%
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，据彭博社今天（11 日）凌晨援引知情人士消息称，受最新 AI 产品需求旺盛推动，OpenAI 第三季度营收首次达到 100 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 668.78 亿元人民币），环比增长近 50%，达到去年同期的近 3 倍。一名知情人士披露，OpenAI 第三季度调整后营业利润率从上一季度的-150% 改善至-109%，亏损幅度有所收窄。此外，OpenAI 在电话会议上透露，截至 9 月底，年化营收规模约为 500 亿美元（现汇率约合 3,343.88 亿元人民币）。今年，OpenAI 在部分指标上曾落后于长期竞争对手 Anthropic，但随着新一代 AI 模型竞争力提升、产品大幅降价，以及业务重心进一步转向帮助客户自动完成工作的 AI 智能体，OpenAI 重新获得增长动力。Anthropic 营收增速开始有所放缓，OpenAI 的业务增长则显现提速迹象。即将登陆美股的 Anthropic 第三季度营收约为 170 亿美元（现汇率约合 1,136.92 亿元人民币），环比增长约 47%，较第二季度超过 140% 的增幅明显放缓。不过，两家公司以往的营收统计口径并不相同。OpenAI 将上市计划推迟至明年，目前正以 1.25 万亿美元（现汇率约合 8.36 万亿元人民币）估值完成新一轮融资。近期，OpenAI 还完成了该轮融资的首批 110 亿美元（现汇率约合 735.65 亿元人民币）融资。Anthropic 则计划于本月晚些时候上市，目标估值为 1.4 万亿美元（现汇率约合 9.36 万亿元人民币）。

articles.title: 开发者 AI 自制工具追踪室内异响，将声源锁定至约 40 厘米范围
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，软件开发者西蒙 · 威利森（Simon Willison）于 11 月 9 日发布博文，借助 AI 编程工具 Claude Code，开发名为 Beep Locator 的声音定位系统，可以将声源锁定至约 40 厘米范围。IT之家援引博文介绍，开发该 Beep Locator 系统的初衷，是威利森搬家后储物室堆积了较多尚未拆封的纸箱，而不时传来短促的“哔哔”电子声。由于鸣叫间隔较长，靠耳朵很难确定来源。于是他借助 Claude Code 编写程序，让分散摆放的五台手机、平板和电脑通过网页调用麦克风，共同捕捉声音。在技术实现方面，该系统主要比较同一声音抵达不同设备的时间差。开发过程中，自动测定设备相对位置的尝试精度不足，威利森便加入手动拖动地图图标、标注设备位置的功能。同时，程序利用快速傅里叶变换分析声音频率，从环境杂音中识别目标提示音，再借助一台设备发出的短音同步各端录音。随着功能逐步完善，系统还能够建议新增设备的摆放位置，帮助进一步缩小搜索范围。最终，威利森按定位结果检查纸箱，找到了发声设备，确认是藏在纸箱里的旧一氧化碳探测器。该项目代码目前已在 GitHub 上公开。参考点此前往 GitHub 访问 Beep Locator 项目

articles.title: 澳大利亚科技教育电子游戏挑战赛将停办，主办方称生成式 AI 加大评审难度
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，曾举办 12 届的澳大利亚 STEM （科技教育）电子游戏挑战赛将在 2026 年举办最后一届。主办方将停办原因归结于生成式 AI 过于普及，以至于评委很难分辨参赛作品是否由学生本人完成。据IT之家了解，澳大利亚 STEM 电子游戏挑战赛创办于 2014 年。这是一项免费赛事，3-12 年级学生可以独立参赛，或组成最多 4 人的团队参赛，开发自己的电子游戏。参赛作品由教师、游戏和科技行业的专业人士进行评审。该比赛主办方 ACER（澳大利亚教育研究委员会）表示，生成式 AI 大大增加了作品评审的难度，也让竞赛偏离了原本的目标。同时，该比赛并没有完全禁止使用生成式 AI。根据官方公布的规则，学生可以借助 AI 编写少量代码，或者排除代码的错误。不过参赛选手必须记录 AI 使用情况，并详细说明使用了什么 AI 工具、用 AI 到底做了什么事。除了最终游戏作品，参赛者还必须提交时长为 1 至 5 分钟的游戏录像，并提供源代码。

articles.title: 腾讯李锐章谈元宝搜索商业模式：不排斥广告，但用户不应该在广告里找答案
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 11 日消息，腾讯全新搜索产品「元宝搜索」今日正式上线，官方宣称元宝搜索优先展示权威机构与官方来源的内容，并将广告与答案明确区分，支持「收起广告」，整块折叠。据新浪科技报道，谈及“元宝搜索”的商业模式，腾讯元宝搜索网页版产品负责人李锐章表示，“作为一款产品，我们并不想完全回避商业关系，但我们的核心思考是，搜索产品的核心使命是给用户提供有价值的结果。”并谈到，“我们不排斥广告，但用户不应该在广告里找答案。”在目前行业普遍做法导致广告与内容边界模糊的情况下，如果处理不好，用户体验可能会隐性下降。对此，我们的想法是‘克制’，并会做好相应的区分。李锐章透露，元宝搜索也在寻找广告与用户需求之间的平衡。“很多时候，广告内容确实能满足用户需求，比如当用户寻找特定服务时，我们会基于用户的当前需求，将相关的产品内容呈现给用户，由用户自行判断和消费。我们希望通过这种更健康的商业模式，与当下的业务任务相结合，追求产品更长久的可持续发展。”据IT之家此前报道，元宝搜索基于元宝的大模型能力，重新构建了从理解、检索、排序到答案组织的整条搜索链路。依托千亿级索引，搜索范围覆盖全网网页、公众号、视频号等腾讯生态内容和学术文献。相关阅读：《腾讯全新搜索产品“元宝搜索”正式上线：能搜微信公众号、视频号，广告与答案明确区分》

articles.content:

Abstract: Closed-loop autonomous experimentation can accelerate scientific discovery, but implementation effort limits accessibility. Agentic systems may lower this barrier, although sustained operation on physical instruments remains largely unexplored. Here, using coding-agent infrastructure grounded in validated scientific methods, we demonstrate autonomous synchrotron X-ray experiments on nanoparticle superlattices under evolving, human-defined objectives. Across three experiments, 61-67% of messages involved interpretation or judgment, while the share of methodological and scientific contributions increased from 46% in the setup-focused first experiment to 56-61% in later experiments. articles.title: EarthRecord: From Pixels to Land Change with Multimodal Agents over Four Decades of Satellite Imagery
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12934v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While multimodal agents now carry out complex data analysis with tools, their ability to turn decades of satellite imagery into reliable land-change analysis, crucial for Earth observation science, remains unmeasured. Existing benchmarks fall short: they pose questions on curated images or give agents preprocessed inputs, leaving out the raw multi-sensor archives where such analysis begins. We introduce EarthRecord, a benchmark built on the raw record of 56 sites: four decades of Landsat, MODIS, VIIRS, and Sentinel-2 data, with cloud masking and cross-sensor harmonization left to the agent. It poses 238 land-change questions across ten analysis tasks, scored against withheld references from global products, agreement among methods, and visual interpretation. articles.title: Train on prefill, monitor at decode: Using sparse autoencoders for topic monitoring
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12935v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Topic monitoring is the task of labelling the topic of each token in a model's response during generation. Activation-based monitors that run at generation time have so far been trained to detect harmful content and are limited to two or three classes. We introduce TopicScope, a framework for training causal topic classifiers on SAE features that assign a topic to every token, so that the label can change partway through a response. We train three detector architectures on synthetic multi-topic conversations covering seven topics. Across Gemma-3 1B and 4B, monitors trained on features extracted from prefill hidden states were able to generalise to decoding. We also found that the classifiers are robust to perturbations, losing at most 5 macro-F1 points when off-topic asides are inserted, topics are removed or sections are reordered. articles.title: LandslideFM: A Foundation Model Towards Unified Landslide Perception and Understanding
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12936v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Intelligent landslide detection is essential for disaster prevention. However, existing models primarily focus on isolated visual tasks, require extensive labeled data, and lack deep analytical and scene-understanding capabilities. To address these limitations, we propose LandslideFM, the first unified foundation model that connects visual perception tasks with contextual interpretation of landslides. Specifically, LandslideFM adapts to multiple visual tasks via a Source-Agreement Graduated Trust semi-supervised learning framework that leverages limited labeled data alongside abundant unlabeled data. Furthermore, predicted landslide regions provide explicit spatial guidance to a Vision-Language Model adapted through parameter-efficient fine-tuning, enabling comprehensive landslide reasoning. articles.title: Tracing Psychometric Inference in Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12937v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Do large language models represent psychological constructs internally, or do they only generate outputs that resemble psychometric structure? We address this question using a cross-persona paradigm across 14 model variants from two families (Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5, 0.5B-14B, base and instruct). Given responses on one psychological scale from real individuals (N = 272 Taiwanese university students), models predict responses on six other scales. At the behavioral level, larger variants reproduce and amplify human cross-scale correlations; amplification persists after correcting the seven-scale human correlations for measurement attenuation. We then examine whether this structure is reflected internally. articles.title: Graph Visualizations in Prompts for Knowledge Graph Question Answering
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12938v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study when and how multimodal input improves knowledge graph question answering (KGQA) in large vision--language models. Using a controlled evaluation over 1,500 WebQSP and CWQ questions and six VLMs within a fixed KGQA pipeline, we compare text-only prompting against text-plus-graph visualization at the per-question level and analyze performance changes as a function of reasoning complexity, model size, and image layout. Adding a graph image yields an average gain of 1.85 F1 points, driven by strong precision improvements on low-complexity questions (+4.65 F1). Mixed-effects and regression analyses show that these multimodal gains do not depend strongly on model scale, but are highly sensitive to graph layout: image-only settings sharply degrade performance, hierarchical Graphviz layouts outperform less organized renderings, and decomposing large subgraphs into separated paths yields the largest improvements. articles.title: AI Governance Should Prioritize Control and Knowledge Boundaries Over Limiting Intelligence
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12941v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The rapid proliferation of autonomously acting AI agents makes the governance of agentic systems urgent. We propose the competence circuit, summarized as IKC + KC + C, that decomposes an agent's real-world impact into three pathways: intelligence-mediated discovery, procedural know-how, and direct control. Using the canonical fast-takeoff debate as a stress test, we formalize the conditions for intelligence-mediated fast takeoff as a conjunction jointly sufficient for fast catastrophic supremacy, showing that most rely on rapid knowledge acquisition or control attainment rather than intelligence alone. We operationalize epistemic intelligence as hypothesis-selection efficiency and validate this framework via stochastic simulation on NK fitness landscapes across six scenarios spanning the conjunctive chain. articles.title: Tabular Foundation Models vs Tuned Gradient Boosting for Telecom Churn: A Profit- and Calibration-Aware Evaluation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12942v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) predict from a labelled context in a single forward pass. A recent benchmark reported that they decisively outperform tree ensembles for customer churn, but it compared them with untuned gradient-boosted trees (GBDTs) and scored only ranking metrics, while a retention campaign is judged in money. We re-evaluate TabPFN-2.5, TabPFN-3.5, TabPFN-3.5-Fast and TabICL v2 against Optuna-tuned GBDTs on five public telecom churn datasets over 10 seeded splits. We separate three questions: whether a model ranks churners well, whether that ranking earns more expected maximum profit (EMP), and whether its probabilities can drive a threshold policy. With a split-aware test and Holm correction over 20 pre-declared comparisons, TabPFN-3.5 earns significantly more EMP than the best tuned GBDT on Cell2Cell (1.9%) and Iranian (7.6%), and these two gains also hold against each of the three tuned GBDTs separately. articles.title: SetPrint: Black-Box LLM Fingerprinting via Setwise Correspondence of Response Changes
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12950v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Black-box LLM fingerprinting aims to determine whether a target model was derived from a source model when only the output responses to input queries are observable. One way to reveal this relationship is to perturb each query and observe the resulting responses of both models, yielding two corresponding sets of response variations. These sets provide two complementary sources of information: the relations among response changes within each set, and the correspondence of response changes between the two sets. Existing approaches, however, have not fully exploited both. We introduce \textbf{SetPrint}, a training-free method that jointly captures both within-set relations and between-set correspondence. SetPrint expresses each response change relative to the mean change of its own set, and then compares changes from the two models that were induced by the same perturbation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12953v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprises increasingly use large language model agents to execute standard operating procedures (SOPs): long, branching, tool-intensive workflows. Yet there is little controlled evidence for choosing among competing agentic architectures. articles.title: Physics2Weight: Direct Neural Network Architecture and Weight Generation from Physical Laws Using Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12954v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled weight-space programming (WSP), which directly generates neural network weights without gradient-based optimization. However, extending WSP to physical problems remains challenging, particularly in achieving both solution accuracy and physical consistency. In this paper, we propose Physics2Weight (PtW), a framework that extends WSP to solving partial differential equations by directly generating neural network weights and editing architectures based on governing equations and initial and boundary conditions. PtW introduces physics-constrained prompting and physics-guided architecture editing, combined with iterative weight refinement from WSP, to improve solution accuracy and physical consistency without gradient-based optimization. articles.title: Embodied Science Agents: Making Embodied Experimental Design Learnable
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12958v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in large models have accelerated AI for Science toward agentic science, where AI agents autonomously conduct scientific discovery. Realising this vision requires closing the loop between computational reasoning and physical experimentation, positioning self-driving laboratories (SDLs) as critical enablers. However, existing SDLs exhibit a fundamental paradox: foundation model integration has increased linguistic sophistication while severing physical grounding. By treating models as disembodied planners that output symbolic workflows for separate robotic systems, current architectures inherently block the development of embodied experimental intuition. We argue that overcoming this paradox requires embedding \emph{learnability} along three interdependent axes: cognitive learnability (learning what to investigate), experimental learnability (learning where to search), and embodied learnability (learning how to act). Abstract: Monitoring a visible channel can change how learned agents communicate without removing why communication is useful. We test this distinction in an end-to-end game where a sender and receiver learn a discrete protocol and route policy without communication supervision. Complete coverage removes most selective migration without removing communication. Frozen interventions, including a fresh pre-outcome confirmation, show that route is semantic: joint message--route shuffling changes .668 of receiver predictions and route alone retains .388 accuracy versus .25 chance. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12961v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Federated fine-tuning with low-rank adaptation (LoRA) reduces communication and computational overhead by training and exchanging compact trainable LoRA factors. Clients may use different LoRA ranks to meet adapter communication budgets and accommodate different local adaptation needs. The server must process these differences during aggregation and construct adapters at each client's rank for local training. We distinguish pre-aggregation alignment, which handles factor dimensions and scaling conventions before aggregation and rank-specific LoRA adapter extraction, which constructs client-sized pairs from the aggregated global model. Two common approaches to rank-specific extraction are direct rank truncation and Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of the dense update. articles.title: BuySideFlow: A Point-in-Time Benchmark for LLM Agents in Investment Research
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12966v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate SQL and SQL--Python workflows for investment research, but ensuring point-in-time (PIT) validity remains challenging. Agents must enforce disclosure cutoffs and select the appropriate historical states and record versions throughout data retrieval and financial analysis. We introduce \textsc{BuySideFlow}, a benchmark of 408 practitioner-derived Chinese-language tasks spanning equities, funds, fixed income, and macroeconomics over a fixed snapshot from a licensed production financial database. We provide executable references and a taxonomy of temporal errors, pairing result checks with expert audits of executed workflows. We evaluate nine agent configurations on all tasks, with result accuracy ranging from 16.2\% to 36.8\%. articles.title: TrustMod-SM: A Multi-Axis Benchmark for Evaluating Trustworthiness of LLMs in Social Media Content Moderation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12970v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) show strong potential for social media content moderation, but their trustworthiness beyond overall accuracy remains underexplored. We introduce TrustMod-SM, a benchmark of roughly 29,000 instances across eight datasets, to evaluate LLM moderators on five dimensions: trustfulness, fairness, safety, robustness, and context integrity. Evaluating 16 open-weight models (0.5B-284B parameters, spanning text-only and vision-language architectures) and one closed frontier model, we find persistent trustworthiness gaps. Higher detection accuracy often coincides with greater demographic disparity, and models frequently comply with concealment or exaggeration prompts, assign high confidence to wrong predictions, rarely escalate ambiguous cases, and struggle to separate hate speech from counter-speech or reclaimed language (especially below 8B parameters). articles.title: ZeroPoint: Lightweight Energy-Based Decision Model
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12992v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Energy-based models (EBMs) assign a scalar energy to every joint value of the observed and predicted variables. In decision models, the prediction is chosen from a finite list of options provided with each input. Inference then reduces to comparing the energies of the options, and training lowers the energy of the correct option relative to the others. A complete decision must also account for the possibility that no option is acceptable. However, the energies learned by a standard EBM define only relative compatibility: adding the same input-dependent quantity to all energies leaves the predictions, the Gibbs distribution, and the usual training losses unchanged. The model therefore has no learned reference level against which to decide whether any option fits. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13006v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) often report a finding because the question names it; standard benchmarks miss this. From public segmentation datasets we build counterfactual views without manual annotation: the lesion erased by inpainting, a same-shape control edit elsewhere, and unedited lesion-free images. The evidence sensitivity gap (ESG) is the rate of absent-or-refer answers after erasure minus the rate after the control edit; it is zero for a model that ignores the image or reacts to both edits alike. articles.title: Predictive Surprise as Self-Grounding Concept Bottleneck for Interpretable Time Series
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12955v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-series classifiers deployed in risk-sensitive domains must be (1) accurate, (2) interpretable, and (3) able to abstain when evidence is weak. Existing methods do not deliver all 3 at once, and the obstacle is structural, rather than logistical. Meaningful temporal patterns cannot be defined without knowing segment boundaries, yet meaningful boundaries cannot be placed without knowing which patterns to expect. Existing approaches break this circularity by using fixed windows or expert-annotated vocabularies, thereby sacrificing at least one of the 3 properties. We introduce ConceptTime, which closes the loop through a single self-supervised signal. A frozen probabilistic forecaster predicts a distribution over the next observation at every timestep of the sequence. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12956v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) reduces the computational cost of attention through token-level selection. However, its indexer still scores the entire causal prefix for each query, making indexing a dominant source of latency in long-context inference. Notably, the indexer alone can account for more than 50% of total prefill GPU time at long context lengths. To address this bottleneck, we propose ADIndex, an Adaptive and Distillation-driven Indexing method for token-level sparse attention. articles.title: Exploration via Exploitation: The Blessing of Reward Diversity in Personalized Federated RL
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12964v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While federated reinforcement learning (RL) has traditionally guaranteed high efficiency in homogeneous environments, collaboration is often hindered when agents possess distinct goals. In this paper, we flip this paradigm, framing reward heterogeneity not as a hurdle to consensus, but as a structural asset that catalyzes exploration. We first propose Personalized Federated Upper Confidence Bound Value Iteration (PF-UCBVI), which achieves optimal linear speedup by decoupling shared dynamics from personalized objectives. To eliminate the risks of explicit exploration, we then introduce Personalized Federated Exploration-Free Value Iteration (PF-EFVI), a purely greedy algorithm that leverages reward diversity to ensure state-action coverage. We prove that PF-EFVI attains logarithmic regret without explicit exploration bonuses under sufficient reward diversity. articles.title: StatPrompt-LLM: A Lightweight Statistical Refinement for Foundation-Style Time-Series Forecasting
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12974v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Time-series forecasting has recently seen a paradigm shift with the introduction of foundation-style models that adapt large pretrained language architectures to sequential data. However, effectively exposing fundamental temporal structures, such as trend, scale, and temporal dependence, to these models remains an open challenge, particularly when the available observations are limited. In this paper, we conduct an exploratory empirical study across different generations of forecasting architectures and propose StatPrompt-LLM, a lightweight statistical refinement of Time-LLM. StatPrompt-LLM augments the existing Time-LLM prompting mechanism with dataset-level statistical information and introduces a zero-initialised autoregressive bypass as a complementary linear forecasting pathway. articles.title: MADSNet: A Multi-Scale Axial-Attentive Dense Spiking Network for Spike Camera Image Reconstruction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12980v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spike cameras encode dynamic scenes into high-temporal-resolution binary spike streams for efficient high-speed vision. Although spiking neural networks (SNNs) can process such signals with sparse and accumulate-only computation, existing SNN-based reconstruction methods are typically shallow and still lag behind ANN-based models in reconstruction fidelity. This paper proposes MADSNet, a Multi-scale Axial-attentive Dense Spiking Network for spike camera image reconstruction. MADSNet adopts a hierarchical spiking encoder--decoder, where a multi-scale spike stem extracts early features, axial spike attention captures long-range dependencies, a dense spiking bottleneck enhances feature reuse, and a spike-to-continuous decoder reconstructs continuous intensity images from spike-domain representations. Experiments on gray-scale and color spike reconstruction show that MADSNet outperforms SSIR by 4.3 dB PSNR and Spk2ImgNet by 1.94 dB on SREDS.

articles.content:

Abstract: Does a useful self-update remain useful after the model updates again? Third Eye separates immediate performance from the outcome of a further native update. We evaluate five 3-8B backbones on math and code: 64 fresh runs, three candidates per run, and three continuations per candidate. Selection and final scoring use disjoint items. In the balanced Qwen3-4B/Llama-3.2-3B comparison, immediate-selected utility is near zero, but continuation reduces it by 1.78 percentage points (simultaneous 95% interval [0.68, 2.88]). Candidate-averaged immediate utility is already negative: selection partly accounts for the apparently neutral first step. Continuation also lowers utility for SmolLM3-3B and Llama-3.1-8B; Qwen3-8B remains inconclusive. Target and out-of-distribution losses dominate retention changes. Abstract: Multimodal attributed graphs (MAGs), in which nodes carry text, images, and other modalities while edges encode relations among entities, underlie e-commerce, social media, content platforms, and creative applications. articles.title: Linear Probes to Bayesian Manifolds: Geometry of Arithmetic in Large Language Models
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Linear probes are a standard method to study geometric structures, such as helices and circles, from the activations of large language models (LLMs), and such structure is often taken as evidence that the model computes with it. Probe accuracy alone cannot establish this, because it conflates four separate claims. These are (1) that the concept is decodable from the activations, (2) that they form a specific shape, (3) that the shape belongs to the probed concept rather than to a related concept the model also represents, and (4) that the output of the model depends on the shape. We call these claims decodability, shape, ownership, and causal use, and we test them separately with a four-stage Bayesian pipeline. Stage 2 compares candidate shapes and selects the best one only when its evidence passes a predefined threshold. articles.content:

Abstract: Generation, imputation, and prediction query different aspects of the same tabular distribution, but are usually evaluated separately. This leaves unclear which capabilities they share, how their training objectives interact, and whether one model can perform all three well. We introduce the One Table Benchmark (\ours{}), spanning 56 datasets, 46 registered methods, and 20 capability axes under aligned data splits and explicit task contracts. We compare task ranks on aligned support, train five backbones under all seven non-empty objective combinations on five datasets with three seeds, and contrast fixed-model profiles with specialist portfolios. Abstract: Reinforcement learning agents are often deployed with policies that cannot be retrained or modified. articles.title: The Shape of a Program: Path Signatures for Trace-to-Program Induction
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13005v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Synthesizing programs from execution traces is a fundamental challenge in algorithmic interpretability and the reverse engineering of complex systems. We bring a rough-path-theoretic perspective to program induction, treating execution traces as high-dimensional rough paths and encoding them with the path signature transform, a tool from stochastic analysis whose expectation provably characterizes the distribution of traces a program induces. On three program-induction domains, Karel, List, and RASP, our log-signature trace encoder outperforms LSTM, Transformer, and Fourier baselines in almost every setting, with its largest margins when training data is scarce. We further observe that the trace-to-program pipeline is naturally contractive: it often produces valid programs that are shorter than the ground truth. Abstract: Synthetic data augmentation promises to scale offline reinforcement learning beyond fixed logged datasets, but leading diffusion-based generators model the transition tuple (state, action, next state, reward, terminal) as a monolith: no single factor can be natively redrawn in isolation. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13057v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Indoor localization commonly combines WiFi received signal strength indicator (RSSI) fingerprints with inertial measurements. However, these sensor streams are sampled asynchronously at different rates; therefore, observations rarely align in time and may be missing or stale. Most existing methods resample the data onto a shared clock and process each modality using a separate branch. We instead present a continuous-time transformer that represents observations as an unordered set of timestamped tokens. Each token encodes its measurement, modality, and elapsed time since acquisition. A single attention block jointly fuses information across modalities and time, avoiding both resampling and modality-specific branches while remaining invariant to token order. Abstract: Brain networks exhibit modular organization, where community structures vary substantially across individuals and diseases. Understanding these individual differences is crucial for advancing both basic neuroscience research and precision medicine. However, widely used predefined group-level brain atlases often overlook this heterogeneity. While individualized functional parcellations capture subject-specific variability in community boundaries, they often require lengthy scan times to achieve fine-grained resolution and complicate cross-subject comparisons. Abstract: Time series from real-world systems are often accompanied by text, such as a report on an event that affects them. Two common tasks on these series are understanding, e.g., answering questions about a series, and forecasting its future values. Both tasks require reasoning over the series and the text together. Moreover, understanding outputs text while forecasting outputs a time series, so serving both requires a model that reads and generates both modalities. Large language models (LLMs) read time series as digit tokens and handle long series poorly. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12903v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Context compression is now routine for language models with long inputs, but a compressed context is useful only if it keeps the evidence for the answer. Existing checks compare the reader model's answer or its most likely words, and thus miss a frequent failure, silent evidence loss: key evidence is removed while the answer stays the same, leaving the answer unsupported and risky for other models that reuse the context. To address this challenge, we propose SELD (Silent Evidence Loss Detector), which needs no training and no labels. Its principle is that when evidence is lost, a reader model's preferences among the answers it leaves unsaid shift even if its answer does not, so comparing these preferences before and after compression reveals losses that answer checks cannot see. articles.title: Capacity Allocation at the Source: Sparse Target Optimization for LLM Knowledge Editing
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12995v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Knowledge editing has emerged as a promising approach for efficiently updating embedded knowledge in large language models (LLMs). It first computes an ideal target hidden state that steers the LLM toward the new output, and then edits the model parameters so that the original hidden state is mapped to this target. While most existing methods focus on the second stage of parameter editing in preserving other knowledge, we find that the upstream construction of the target hidden state also plays an important role in allocating the model's limited capacity space. We first establish a theoretical connection between interference in the parameter space and interference between target hidden states, showing that the two are positively correlated. Building on this insight, we propose a simple yet effective $\ell_1$ regularization method that prunes away unnecessary ``tentacles'' of each knowledge vector, retaining only the essential components.

Abstract: Thai is written without spaces between words, making segmentation a foundational step in most Thai NLP pipelines. articles.title: Understanding Students' Rationales for AI-Mediated Cheating: An Instructor Perspective from Online Forums Analysis
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13358v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The extensive adoption of AI has precipitated a crisis in academic integrity. While studies attempt to quantify cheating, less is known about the motivations instructors believe students have for using AI in prohibited ways. We analyze 2.01 million posts on r/Professors to understand how instructors perceive students' justifications for AI-mediated cheating. Our qualitative analyses reveal four primary themes: (1) Academic System Gaming, (2) Digital-Academic Literacy Gap, (3) Performance Anxiety, and (4) Normalization of Dishonesty.

Abstract: In teaching and learning environments, cheating and the violation of academic integrity have always been one of the challenges, involving different levels of concerns such as administrative, personal knowledge, learning, and equity. The introduction of large language models has brought cheating in dialogue to the forefront, given the apparent capabilities of these models to complete students' academic assignments. In doing so, we analyze a corpus of 2.01 million posts (threads and comments) in the r/Professors subreddit discussing cheating after the release of ChatGPT, providing a better understanding of teachers' motivations to discourage cheating and the strategies they use to do so. articles.content:

Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated considerable potential in biomedical applications, while agentic memory systems have emerged as a promising approach to preserving and utilizing information across tasks and interactions. Abstract: Most language models deployed outside the United States and China are fine-tuned descendants of a small number of pretrained families. We argue that fine-tuning leaves the decisive properties of a model inherited from its base: vocabulary, knowledge, cultural alignment, memorized data and license. Abstract: Reconstructing high-fidelity LiDAR simulation scenes from real-world driving logs is essential for cost-effective safety validation of autonomous driving systems. Abstract: Generalized category discovery (GCD) aims to discover novel categories from unlabeled data by leveraging limited labeled samples from old classes. To this end, we propose AptM-GCD, a novel multimodal framework that exploits apt textual guidance through attribute evidence learning and multimodal prompt reasoning. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12976v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Open-vocabulary object detection (OVD) expects the model trained on base classes to recognize both base and novel classes at inference. Typical methods rely on CLIP-style vision-language embeddings, yet the learned space is often biased toward base categories, with limited effective capacity preserved for novel concepts. Such a base-dominated representation can compress novel semantics, leading to semantic collapse and mis-calibrated confidence at inference. To address this issue, we present PR-OVD, a partition-and-refine framework that explicitly reserves capacity for novel categories and strengthens category separation, while being seamlessly integrated into different detector architectures. Abstract: Surgical action-center localization requires both an accurate reference point and a decision about whether to report it. When frames with and without a reportable center are mixed, the benefit of improved localization depends on which correct candidates survive selection. We present a selective localization pipeline combining heatmap and coordinate supervision with a logistic-regression scorer. The scorer learns to identify predictions with a reportable center and a localization error within a specified tolerance. The internal evaluation uses 5,000 frames from 50 surgical sources, five source-grouped folds and two random seeds. Matched locator and scoring comparisons track correct candidates and their rejection. articles.title: Trajectory-Regularized Distribution Distillation for One-Step Generation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12978v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Distilling flow matching models for one-step generation generally follows two paradigms. Trajectory alignment supervises the student with the teacher's probability flow ODE, but its performance degrades under very small sampling budgets. Distribution matching directly optimizes the generated distribution, but estimating its reverse Kullback-Leibler gradient typically requires a separate network to track the evolving student score. We propose trajectory-regularized distribution distillation (TRD), which combines distribution-level and trajectory-level supervision through a momentum-mixture policy predicted in a single student forward pass. This policy serves simultaneously as a one-step generator, an estimator of the student's marginal velocity that removes the need for a second trainable network in distribution matching, and a closed-form time-dependent velocity field supervised along the teacher ODE trajectory. articles.content:

Abstract: Overlapping imaging manifestations complicate the differential diagnosis of Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases (DCLDs), while limited annotated data constrain supervised model development. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) can integrate imaging and clinical information, but their diagnostic reasoning remains limited by incomplete volumetric perception and insufficient grounding in disease-specific evidence. Abstract: Multimodal (e.g. vision-language, in this work) attribution aims to interpret the models without access to ground-truth explanatory supervision. Existing multimodal attribution methods typically rely on paired modalities as proxy supervision, implicitly assuming that image-text pairs are semantically aligned. Information bottleneck (IB)-based attribution methods follow this general paradigm and instantiate it through a global sufficiency-compression objective. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13004v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Discrete autoregressive models offer a scalable framework for image generation. However, they face a fundamental trade-off: long token sequences preserve representation quality but slow generation, while aggressive spatial compression reduces representation capacity. Based on product quantization, we show that, under a fixed nominal information budget, group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor. Abstract: Complete-or-reject reporting of surgical action triplets can discard a correctly identified instrument and action when the target is uncertain. We introduce instance-preserving graded semantic reporting, which separates instance selection from the choice of semantic detail. Each selected instance retains its predicted mask and labels while hierarchical correctness scores guide instrument (I), instrument-verb (IV), or complete instrument-verb-target (IVT) reporting. The utility-increment rule DELTA weighs the expected gain from finer reporting against its error cost. We compare three decision rules on 5,641 test frames from eight surgical videos using fixed predictions and scores. Abstract: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). A web server provides access to the online environment and evaluation interface, supporting parallel testing through screenshots and keyboard-mouse actions with automatic engine-state outcome checks. articles.title: Maze Runner: Autonomous Maze Navigation with Line-Based Localization and Control Barrier Functions
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12949v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Maze navigation requires localization from sparse, repetitive geometry, planning through narrow corridors, and control that stays safe when the estimate or the map is wrong. We present Maze Runner, an open autonomy stack in C++ and ROS 2 that addresses these needs end to end on a simulated Husarion ROSbot XL with a 2D LiDAR in Gazebo. Perception extracts wall lines from each scan with RANSAC and total least squares, with per-line uncertainty. The same line front end feeds two estimators: an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) that localizes against a line map built from the maze mesh, and an EKF SLAM variant that builds the line map online. arXiv:2611.13034v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Robot agents can improve reusable skills, planning procedures, and recovery strategies from execution feedback, yet a fixed practice source leaves the search for new weaknesses unchanged. Useful practice depends on the agent's current capabilities, so the procedure that chooses practice must also be revisable. We present RoboACE (Robot Adversarial Co-Evolution), a framework that jointly evolves curriculum and execution harnesses around frozen foundation models. The curriculum harness uses accumulated capability evidence to propose informative challenges, while the execution harness responds with reusable revisions that expand execution capabilities. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13039v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reliable medical laboratory automation requires robots to complete entire workflows in protocol order while handling changes during execution. A robot may execute each motion correctly yet fail the workflow by confusing visually similar stages or stalling after human intervention. We present Robo-MLT, a dual-system framework that couples explicit workflow monitoring with learned action generation. A vision--language planner composes an ordered atomic-skill sequence from the protocol and the initial workspace observation. A multiframe execution monitor detects when the active skill has completed or become infeasible, then advances the workflow or triggers replanning. A skill-conditioned vision--language--action policy generates the manipulation trajectories, and an asynchronous runtime coordinates it with the monitor. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13114v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: System identification requires expert decisions on the identification method, incorporation of prior physical knowledge, and model validation. We propose ASPIRE, a framework for nonlinear system identification in which a large language model agent selects and executes the identification method. ASPIRE constructs closed-form, nonlinear static or dynamic models from measured data, optionally supplemented by a system description, the intended use of the model, and physical requirements expressed formally or in natural language. Each model includes its parameters, an estimation record, an interpretation of its terms, and an error evaluated on test data inaccessible to the agent. Formal physical requirements are verified independently. ASPIRE operates autonomously or interactively, allowing the agent to ask questions and the user to request further analyses and identification rounds. Abstract: Learning-based decentralized collision avoidance must remain reliable under state-estimation uncertainty and heterogeneous agent dynamics. Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models now exceed 95% success on the LIBERO simulation benchmark, yet it remains unclear how much of this performance requires generalization beyond the training demonstrations. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13204v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Many rehabilitation robots execute prescribed motions using reactive tracking controllers that do not explicitly incorporate the user's instantaneous human-ground interaction. This paper presents Ground Reaction Force-Aware Model Predictive Control (GRF-MPC), a framework for upright physical assistance. By integrating live GRF and center of pressure (CoP) measurements directly into a human centroidal dynamics model, GRF-MPC formulates a real-time quadratic program (QP) that optimizes assistive forces and moments over a receding horizon. We deployed GRF-MPC on the Robotic Upright Stand Trainer (RobUST) in an underactuated 4-cable configuration and evaluated it against a fully actuated 8-cable Cartesian impedance baseline in nearly 300 trials across six healthy participants. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13227v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce Latent Barrier Steering (LBS), a hierarchical semantic-to-path framework for safe flow-matching-based generative planning. Existing control-barrier-function (CBF) safety filters for diffusion and flow-matching planners act locally on generated samples, either during sampling or after prediction. Such repair is effective for small violations, but can struggle when a new constraint blocks the whole selected behavior mode rather than merely perturbing it locally. LBS decouples behavior selection from path certification through two coordinated interventions: it first steers the generator's behavior latent toward rollouts with larger safety margin, then decodes the steered latent and applies a path-space CBF quadratic program (QP) only for residual violations. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13229v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Efficient robotic 3D reconstruction requires selecting views that contribute new surface measurements with few physical captures. Pretrained world models can guide this choice, but a predicted surface may not produce valid depth measurements under the operating conditions of the deployed sensor. We present a deployment adaptation methodology for next-best-view selection that learns a sensor-return adapter from limited local calibration data while keeping the pretrained predictor fixed. The adapter estimates measurement dropout over each predicted surface, allowing the selection method to favor views likely to fill gaps in the measured reconstruction. arXiv:2611.13251v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A person running a bench experiment works from a printed instruction sheet, tells identical containers apart by the labels written on them, and looks at the bench again before each step. Lab automation usually works the other way around: the procedure is written as a script, and containers stand at fixed positions or carry fiducial markers. We present Curie's Jarvis, a system that lets a robot arm carry out a chemistry experiment on a bench set up for people. It reads the steps from a photo of the printed sheet, finds containers on an ordinary bench with no fixed positions or markers, tells identical-looking containers apart by reading their labels in four camera views, locates its target again before every step, and sets how each step is carried out, including its speed, from what is being handled. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13268v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In cooperative object manipulation, the placement of pushing contacts determines whether force closure can be achieved and agents can generate arbitrary forces and torques on the object correspondingly. This study derives a necessary and sufficient closed-form condition for the planar force closure of a rectangular object, a common object shape in everyday settings, under four frictionless pushing contacts. For a rectangle of length $b$ and width $a$, force closure holds if and only if $(l_1+l_3-b)(l_2+l_4-a)<0$, where $l_1,l_2,l_3,l_4$ are the four edge contact locations. This condition is independent of the object's center of mass and is used to verify contact configurations before contact force allocation. When the condition is not satisfied, the signs of the two factors indicate which opposing contact pair should be adjusted. Abstract: Planning planetary rover trajectories under probabilistic uncertainty is a multi-objective optimization problem that science teams currently iteratively solve and verify by hand. This process becomes impractical when timelines and constraints frequently shift throughout the mission planning phase. Sampling-based planners such as Monte Carlo tree search can speed up this process, but their outputs do not preserve traceability to the science objectives that justify each plan, which the science team needs to verify. We propose an interactive assistant based on a large language model (LLM) that can explain planner trajectories using domain vocabulary and re-run the planner under user-specified conditions to compare alternatives. Abstract: A humanoid that dances to streamed music must commit each motion chunk before it has heard the music that chunk accompanies, and must continue from motion it has already committed. ListenAhead conditions each chunk on heard music and a frozen music model's forecasts of the coming music, aligned to their target times and weighted by reliability. Abstract: Decision making in multi-agent and multi-robot systems often involves discrete decision variables, leading to NP-hard combinatorial optimization problems that must be solved within seconds for near real-time implementation. articles.title: Rhythmic-Semantic Co-Speech Gestures for Emotional Dialogue in Robots
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13472v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Co-speech gestures can increase engagement and improve speech understanding. Yet, most data-driven robot systems generate either rhythmic beat-like motion or semantically meaningful iconic gestures, but not both. We present an emotion-aware rhythmic-semantic co-speech gesture system that generates iconic and beat behaviors in real time from text and the robot's internal emotional state. We formalize the task of beat-iconic gesture generation using emotion and propose lightweight models that predict iconic timing and intensity, then fill the remaining spans with emotion-conditioned beats at an appropriate intensity level. We train on the BEAT2 dataset and deploy the system on the social robot Haru. In an online user study with 60 participants, our method shows stronger speech-gesture alignment and is preferred over baseline methods.

Not petty change for everyone.I was surprised when i asked for the transcripts/recordings for some of these conferences so i could do a brain dump at teh end of the day. I learned to my surprise that these were not available even to the attendees. Why? I dunno. I asked the staff at the desk and they mentioned something about youtube release and engagement. But really they had no idea why not release them at least for the attendees. Not their fault. They did graciously offer to forward my concern up the chain. Thank you to them.I have ADHD specifically I have memory encoding issues. For me context(no pun intended) is literally ephemeral and i would like to convert what i learned today to important facts else it will go poof in 48-96 hours.

articles.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
articles.content: Foundation models pretrained on large natural-image collections are increasingly adapted for medical image segmentation, in the expectation that they will replace models trained for each task. Most comparisons, however, use data from the training distribution and a single task-specific baseline whose configuration is rarely justified, and therefore provide limited evidence of performance at new clinical sites. It also remains unclear how much of a foundation model must be adapted, and what determines this. We adapted a foundation model, DINOv2, with strategies ranging from tuning only its bias terms to full fine-tuning, and compared it with U-Nets and ResU-Nets trained from scratch. Experiments covered colonoscopy, breast ultrasound and dermoscopy, with testing on held-out data from the training source and on independent datasets from other institutions. The adapted foundation model generalised better on every external dataset. Within the training distribution, the task-specific models remained competitive when training data were abundant, and delineated boundaries more precisely, while the foundation model more often missed small lesions. Only a small fraction of the foundation model required adaptation, and the capacity needed was determined by the imaging domain rather than by the adaptation method. A widely used polyp test set was also found to duplicate images from another benchmark. Foundation-model adaptation is therefore warranted where models must work across sites, with capacity selected on the target domain.

articles.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
articles.content: DeepLearning (DL)-based Computer-Aided Diagnostic (CAD) systems have shown great promise in supporting clinicians, but their performance heavily depends on the availability of large, well-annotated datasets. In medical lesion detection, the scarcity of comprehensive, stan dardized annotations and the heterogeneity of existing datasets limit the development of robust foundation models. In this work, we introduce a novel approach to building a multi-domain foundation model for le sion detection by integrating diverse medical image datasets annotated for both anatomical structures and abnormalities. We first propose a student-teacher training strategy to effectively combine datasets with heterogeneous label spaces, mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and im proving feature learning. In addition, building on our previously pro posed example-based EM-DETR framework, we adapt it to jointly learn from multiple domain-specific datasets, enabling fine-grained, example driven detection across modalities. Our model achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) results, with image-level AUC scores exceeding previous SOTA by 1% point on four key findings in CXRs. We achieve a leading mAP50 in CXRs and mammography, surpassing EM-DETR trained on a single dataset by 2-3% points. This approach paves the way for scalable foundation models in medical imaging that leverage heterogeneous data while maintaining robust and generalizable performance.

articles.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
articles.content: We present TorchCurves, a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives. Its central operation maps batches of scalar inputs to points on curves represented in B-spline or Legendre polynomial bases, with differentiation through both inputs and coefficients. Curve coefficients can be optimized jointly with the surrounding model or produced by another network. The library provides trainable modules, reusable basis modules, and a functional interface, supporting applications ranging from continuous feature embeddings to Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and functional regression. Its implementation combines classical evaluation algorithms with vectorized PyTorch operations, emphasizing readability and maintainability without custom hardware kernels. Timing experiments compare curve evaluation against NumPy and SciPy and KAN training against EfficientKAN across a range of problem sizes. The results illustrate where this generality remains computationally practical and where overhead is substantial. Library is available on GitHub at https://github.com/alexshtf/torchcurves.

articles.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
articles.content: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) produces rich training experience, yet outcome rewards reduce each attempt to a single number and leave most of this information unused. Training-time scaffolds, such as strategies or hints added to the prompt during training, offer a natural way to turn this information into guidance, but their design and adaptation are largely left to humans and tailored to specific domains. We introduce AutoScaffold, a unified AI-for-AI framework that turns a student's training experience into adaptive scaffolds, with minimal domain-specific information and no human intervention during training. A frozen teacher periodically examines this experience, diagnoses bottlenecks, and designs scaffolds in two forms: (i) strategies shared across a class of tasks and (ii) hints for individual hard tasks, adjusting the content and amount of support as the student learns. The scaffolds are removed at evaluation. We apply the same framework to ALFWorld, search-based QA, mathematical reasoning, and GPU kernel generation. When evaluated without scaffolds, students trained with AutoScaffold outperform those trained with the corresponding RL baselines in all four domains, with gains of 7.2 points in ALFWorld success and 4.0 points in average QA exact match. On GPU kernel generation, AutoScaffold increases the fraction of tasks with a correct kernel that runs faster than the PyTorch reference by up to 5.0 points. On math, our student surpasses QuestA's reported accuracy using approximately one-third as many student training steps. Analyses show that the teacher identifies a different failure in each task class and shifts its scaffolds from step-by-step workflows to targeted fixes as the student improves, and that its revised scaffolds help the student learn more than keeping the previous scaffold or using no scaffold.

articles.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
articles.content: LLM agents are increasingly used for open-ended, data-driven scientific discovery, yet most of them evaluate hypotheses pointwise, testing an empirical claim $h$ only against its complement $\neg h$. When evidence rejects $h$, the agent learns that one explanation is unlikely but not which alternative the evidence supports. To recover that alternative, we introduce Contrastive Discovery, which replaces the single hypothesis with a contrast set, a scientific question paired with mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive competing explanations. Each experiment is scored by how its evidence redistributes belief across the set, and the question is resolved when belief concentrates on one explanation. Because contrast sets change only the unit an agent proposes and scores, an existing agent can use them to re-evaluate evidence it has already collected or to guide its search. Across six domains, $89\%$ of the pointwise candidates with the largest belief shifts are rejections. On the same evidence, contrast sets resolve $73\%$ of these candidates to a specific alternative. When contrast sets guide search, the agent resolves $67\%$ more questions than pointwise surprisal under the same experiment budget. In a blinded study, $38$ human experts chose the same explanation on $78\%$ of resolved questions and on $82\%$ of questions where the pointwise agent rejected its hypothesis and stopped. Together, these results support explicit competing explanations as a way for discovery agents to resolve more scientific questions from the same evidence and validation budget.

articles.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
articles.content: Predicting how a ligand binds to its target is central to small-molecule drug discovery. Modern cofolding models can generate diverse candidate poses, but reliably ranking these candidates remains challenging. We introduce Pyrite, a pairwise pose-ranking benchmark comprising 1,500 pose pairs across diverse protein-ligand complexes. Expert chemists equipped with 3D visualization tools and physics-based scores perform near chance, highlighting the difficulty of interpreting available chemical signals. To investigate automated ranking, we introduce PyriteRep, a structured representation of molecular geometry, protein-ligand interactions, and physicochemical scores, and develop two LLM-based agents: PyriteReasoner, which directly compares poses through text-based reasoning, and PyriteFeaturizer, which generates executable code to construct features for logistic regression, optionally incorporating features derived from LLM subcalls. These agents achieve up to 67% and 74% accuracy, respectively, exceeding observed expert performance. LLM-guided feature discovery generally outperforms direct reasoning, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) improves open-weight models, enabling them to match or surpass closed-source frontier models in our evaluations. These results establish Pyrite as a challenging test of pose-ranking ability and highlight LLM-guided feature discovery as a promising approach to interpret and combine the outputs of computational chemistry tools.

articles.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
articles.content: Connectome-constrained models are often used to argue that a measured wiring diagram outperforms shuffled or rewired wiring, and hence that structure shapes function. Such comparisons can confound wiring with how the models are tuned: a connectome fixes who connects to whom, not the excitability, gains or plasticity rates the model also needs, and modellers often tune these until the real-wiring model works. We separate three estimands: physiology tuned on the real wiring and transferred to nulls (P1), each wiring tuned on its own (P2), and P2 restricted to physiology consistent with independent data (P3). The biases involved are known in machine learning (under-tuned baselines, inherited weights, winner's curse); we measure what they do to biological conclusions, using synthetic ground truth, placebo nulls and three Drosophila circuit models. Some claims survive every protocol we test: segregated reward and punishment dopamine improves learning, and head-direction topography is required for a persistent bump. Others do not. In the mushroom body, the real Kenyon-cell output wiring beats a cross-subtype identity shuffle by 0.09 under P1 and P2 but loses to it by 0.09 under P3 (95% CIs exclude zero; held-out runs confirm). The verdict is set by the share of alpha'beta' cells among active Kenyon cells, which P1 selects low; at the share implied by imaging (about 44%) the real-wiring model fails to learn, exposing a model inadequacy rather than a deficit of the fly's wiring. In flyvis, P1 penalises a mirrored connectome, which has a constructed solution within 0.07 (median) of the real error, more than a spatially shuffled one in 50 of 50 members; the ranking survives ten-fold longer retraining but depends on the checkpoint at fifty-fold. A credible structural claim needs matched optimisation, data-constrained physiology and a model that still works there.

articles.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
articles.content: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. The same tasks return after dormant gaps with fresh instances, while new tasks keep arriving. On each instance, the learner may pay for demonstrations, submit answers, or act inside the harness, with retries permitted on incorrect submissions, which are paid for. Each instance is scored based on the share of this feedback budget consumed. Since a learner may keep anything between instances, memory-based and weight-based systems are scored on the same scale. After the stream, the learner is frozen and tested on fresh instances of the tasks it met, which measures memorization, and on unseen tasks, which measures generalization. We run an agent harness with frozen weights, with and without persistence, on Qwen3.5-9B and GLM-5.3 Flash, comparing them with two prompting floors, a program-induction method and Qwen3.5-9B's weights trained to imitate GLM-5.3 Flash. Persistence in the harness generally does not improve memorization unless provided with explicit expert guidance. Most harness-based methods still learn less than a floor that simply caches each task's demonstrations, across all models we tested. No harness-based method gains on unseen tasks, whereas weight-based learning shows substantial gains. This opens the door to future weight-based continual learning that could teach models to drive harnesses in new domains.

articles.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
articles.content: Foundation models trained on large unlabeled corpora develop emergent capabilities, tasks that go beyond the training objective. We extend this paradigm to multimodal biology with Bonbon, a foundation model for molecular interactions trained on approximately 3.2 trillion tokens of paired protein-ligand sequences. From a single representation space, Bonbon exhibits three zero-shot emergent capabilities at hierarchical levels of resolution: functional (mechanism of action), residue (binding site localization, including orthosteric/allosteric discrimination), and bond (covalent versus non-covalent engagement). All three capabilities generalize to out-of-distribution complexes. Bonbon was trained on protein-ligand sequences alone, without any task-specific supervision and without structural coordinates. We conducted controlled scaling experiments across six model scales from 42M to 1.6B parameters; every capability evaluated shows a sharp jump at the largest scale on continuous metrics, even as pretraining loss decreases smoothly. This demonstrates that loss-based scaling laws alone are insufficient to predict when zero-shot emergent capabilities become available. The capabilities reported here emerge after training at a 1:2,000 parameter-to-token ratio to accommodate the sparsity of paired biological interaction data. The same frozen representations achieve state-of-the-art binding and affinity prediction at five orders of magnitude greater speed than co-folding methods. In prospective wet-lab validation across nine disease targets spanning seven protein families, Bonbon achieves a 61.5% dose-response hit rate on de novo compounds, yielding structurally novel molecules not previously reported to inhibit these proteins, including for out-of-distribution targets.

articles.title: Measuring Robustness and Efficiency in a Connectome-Constrained Fly Visual System Model: Linking an Adversarial and a Perceptual Illusion
articles.content: Biological visual systems compute reliably under tight metabolic and wiring constraints, whereas artificial vision systems consume far more energy and can be sensitive to adversarial perturbations. Whether networks with brain-like wiring are more robust at lower computational cost is unclear. We address this by benchmarking a task-optimized, continuous-time recurrent neural network of the fly visual system constrained by its synaptic connectome (FlyNet) against artificial neural networks. We compare it against CNNs, RAFT, and continuous-time recurrent neural networks without detailed connectome constraints (sCTRNN, CTRNN) on a collision-detection task within a differentiable 3D rendering pipeline. FlyNet is adversarially vulnerable but, relative to its compute, more robust to common video corruptions than RAFT, while using up to five orders of magnitude fewer FLOPs. The CTRNNs remain more robust than FlyNet across almost all tested perturbations, suggesting that connectome constraints benefit efficiency, through their low edge count, over robustness. Recurrence improves robustness to white-box attacks in RAFT and temporal context improves robustness to common corruptions. FlyNet's position and velocity representations degrade under adversarial textures but recover under counterfactual textures that restore correct classification while staying equally far from training, ruling out unfamiliar textures as the cause of failure. The reverse-phi illusion similarly disrupts these representations and inverts the same low-level motion statistic as the adversarial textures. Optimizing this input statistic alone, without access to the network, suffices to induce classification failure, attributing both perturbations to the same circuit vulnerability. Connectome-constrained models can thus surface adversarial failure mechanisms as testable hypotheses about biological perceptual vulnerabilities.
